2607.01047.title: Conversable Complexity: Agentic LLM Collectives as Interpretable Substrates
2607.01047.paper_summary: Complexity and interpretability rarely coincide: systems rich enough for complex behaviours to emerge are usually too opaque to question, while transparent ones are too simple for anything complex to emerge. A single large language model (LLM) is a static artefact, hardly exhibiting any of the emergent properties we associate with life. This changes through interaction: populations of LLMs display emergent dynamics absent from isolated models. Furthermore, LLMs can be endowed with persistent memory, tools and shared skills, and the capacity to initiate actions unprompted, i.e., turning LLMs agentic. In this paper, we argue that such collectives of agents can serve as a computational substrate for Artificial Life (ALife) research. Critically, since the agents communicate in natural language, their collective behaviour can be directly interrogated by examining textual traces and asking the agents themselves. We outline the notion of interpretability in language-model research and extend it for collectives of agents. Lastly, we survey recent examples of agentic LLM collectives that already instantiate the idea of agentic substrates, from controlled experiments to deployments in the wild.
2607.01047.paper_summary_zh: 複雜性和可解釋性很少同時存在：足夠豐富以產生複雜行為的系統通常過於不透明而無法質疑，而透明的系統則過於簡單，無法產生任何複雜的現象。單一的大型語言模型（LLM）是一個靜態的產物，幾乎不展現我們與生命相關的任何突現特性。這種情況通過互動而改變：LLM的群體顯示出孤立模型所缺乏的突現動態。此外，LLM可以被賦予持久的記憶、工具和共享技能，以及在未經提示的情況下啟動行動的能力，即使LLM變得具有代理性。在本文中，我們主張這樣的代理集體可以作為人工生命（ALife）研究的計算基底。關鍵是，由於這些代理以自然語言進行交流，它們的集體行為可以通過檢查文本痕跡和詢問代理本身來直接探究。我們概述了語言模型研究中可解釋性的概念，並將其擴展到代理集體。最後，我們調查了已經體現代理基底概念的代理LLM集體的最近例子，從受控實驗到野外部署。
